A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoAL research. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison, including the new Appendix A in v2; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original active-learning experiments on six datasets, component and candidate-pool ablations, and strategy-selection analyses in Figures 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments, adds TinyImageNet and additional baseline results, and reports original runtime measurements in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The FitNet/SearchNet architecture, seven candidate strategies, Gaussian-mixture scoring, sigmoid relaxation, objectives and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added description of SearchNet's sample-wise output explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds TinyImageNet, extending natural-image classification coverage to a 200-class dataset. The original six datasets and medical-image tasks remain. Newly documented imbalance ratios do not establish additional imbalanced-data experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds evaluated DDU, Coreset, VAAL and ENSvarR comparisons across the retained benchmarks, substantially expanding the baseline set beyond the original ten methods. Coreset was previously cited but not evaluated; Meta-Query Net remains discussion only.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces a timing protocol measuring the complete AL process, including training and querying, normalized to EntropySampling and divided into AutoAL components. Existing dataset splits, ResNet-18 models, learning rates and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a substantial computational-cost analysis across seven datasets, including candidate-scoring, search and classifier-training costs, plus a reported three-candidate runtime comparison. This newly examines computational bottlenecks and candidate-pool tradeoffs. The original ablations and strategy-score analyses in Figures 3–5 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions with different randomly selected initial labeled pools and report mean accuracy and standard deviation. V2 introduces no new run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure; its runtime table reports averages.

E6.justification: V2 adds TinyImageNet accuracy curves, results for four additional baselines on the original datasets, and the runtime results in Table 2. AutoAL's total runtime is reported as 2.95–6.54 times EntropySampling's. The matched original accuracy curves and ablation results are retained, rather than showing revised AutoAL performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(9) remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof. The new complexity appendix presents empirical timings, not a mathematical complexity derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the claims of differentiable AL strategy search, efficient optimization, flexibility and superior performance across natural and medical images. The expanded experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly interprets candidate scoring as the main computational bottleneck and discusses choosing fewer or faster candidates to balance accuracy and cost. The new Impact Statement also asserts bias mitigation and fair selection without corresponding fairness analysis. Existing mechanism interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The code statement changes from a promised release to reported availability. V2 additionally identifies a single Nvidia A100 for the timing experiments and documents dataset imbalance ratios. Existing implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds a brief Meta-Query Net discussion, cites Zhao et al. for Gaussian-mixture-related AL motivation, and adds references associated with TinyImageNet and new baselines. The main positioning relative to adaptive AL and bilevel optimization is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local wording corrections, a short SearchNet-output explanation, acknowledgements, an Impact Statement and the new appendix, rather than extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main paper from single-column to two-column ICML formatting, substantially reflowing equations and displays. Figure 2 expands from six to seven panels with a larger legend; Table 1 moves to the appendix and gains a dataset row and imbalance column; runtime Table 2 is new.

improvement.justification: The expanded Figure 2 comparisons and Appendix A.1 improve empirical scrutiny and reveal previously undocumented computational costs. These gains are qualified: Table 2 shows AutoAL slower than many baselines despite retained broad efficiency claims, and the new fairness assurance lacks supporting analysis. The revision therefore offers a useful but limited overall quality improvement.
